title: Stoichiometry of Gaseous Substances, Mixtures, and Reactions
lead: The ideal gas law turns measurements of pressure, volume and temperature into an amount of gas, and this section puts that to work. It finds the density and the molar mass of a gas, adds the partial pressures of the gases in a mixture by Dalton’s law, corrects a gas collected over water for the water vapor it holds, and uses volumes of gases in the stoichiometry of reactions.
objectives: Use the ideal gas law to compute gas densities and molar masses
Perform stoichiometric calculations involving gaseous substances
State Dalton’s law of partial pressures and use it in calculations involving gaseous mixtures
summary_html: The ideal gas law can be used to derive a number of convenient equations relating directly measured quantities to properties of interest for gaseous substances and mixtures. Appropriate rearrangement of the ideal gas equation may be made to permit the calculation of gas densities and molar masses. Dalton’s law of partial pressures may be used to relate measured gas pressures for gaseous mixtures to their compositions. Avogadro’s law may be used in stoichiometric computations for chemical reactions involving gaseous reactants or products.

(Figure 9.21) When a reaction produces a gas that is collected above water, the trapped gas is a mixture of the gas produced by the reaction and water vapor. If the collection flask is appropriately positioned to equalize the water levels both within and outside the flask, the pressure of the trapped gas mixture will equal the atmospheric pressure outside the flask (see the earlier discussion of manometers). (Figure 9.22) This graph shows the vapor pressure of water at sea level as a function of temperature.

exercises.prompt: What is the density of molecular hydrogen gas at 17.0 °C and a pressure of 760 torr?

answer.hint: Convert to kelvin and atmospheres, then use d = ℳP/RT with the molar mass of H₂.

exercises.prompt: Acetylene, a fuel used in welding torches, is composed of 92.3% C and 7.7% H by mass. Find the empirical formula. If 1.10 g of acetylene occupies of volume of 1.00 L at 1.15 atm and 59.5 °C, what is the molecular formula for acetylene?

answer.solution: Empirical formula, CH; Molecular formula, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>

exercises.prompt: A sample of phosphorus that weighs 3.243 × 10<sup>−2</sup> g exerts a pressure of 31.89 kPa in a 56.0-mL bulb at 550 °C. What are the molar mass and molecular formula of phosphorus vapor?

answer.hint: Use ℳ = mRT/PV with the pressure in atm, the volume in L and the temperature in K, then compare with the atomic mass of phosphorus.

exercises.prompt: A 5.73-L flask at 25 °C contains 0.0388 mol of N<sub>2</sub>, 0.147 mol of CO, and 0.0803 mol of H<sub>2</sub>. What is the total pressure in the flask in atmospheres?

answer.hint: Add the amounts of the three gases, then use P = nRT/V for the total.

exercises.prompt: What is the pressure of a mixture of 0.200 g of H<sub>2</sub>, 1.00 g of N<sub>2</sub>, and 0.820 g of Ar in a container with a volume of 2.00 L at 20 °C?

answer.hint: Convert each mass to moles, add them, and use P = nRT/V.

exercises.prompt: A sample of oxygen collected over water at a temperature of 29.0 °C and a pressure of 764 torr has a volume of 0.560 L. What volume would the dry oxygen from this sample have under the same conditions of temperature and pressure?

answer.hint: Subtract the vapor pressure of water at 29.0 °C from the total to find the pressure of the oxygen alone, then use Boyle’s law.

exercises.prompt:
An acetylene tank for an oxyacetylene welding torch provides 9340 L of acetylene gas, C2H2, at 0 °C and 1 atm. How many tanks of oxygen, each providing 7.00 × 103 L of O2 at 0 °C and 1 atm, will be required to burn the acetylene?
$2{\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{2}+5{\text{O}}_{2}\;\longrightarrow \;4{\text{CO}}_{2}+2{\text{H}}_{2}\text{O}$

answer.hint: The volumes react in the ratio of the coefficients, 2 to 5; divide the volume of oxygen by the volume one tank provides.

exercises.prompt: What volume of O2(g) measured at 25 °C and 760 torr is required to react with 17.0 L of ethylene, C2H4(g), measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure? The products are CO2 and water vapor.

answer.hint: Balance the combustion of ethylene; the volumes react in the ratio of the coefficients.

exercises.prompt: Sulfur dioxide is an intermediate in the preparation of sulfuric acid. What volume of SO<sub>2</sub> at 343 °C and 1.21 atm is produced by burning 1.00 kg of sulfur in excess oxygen?

answer.hint: Find the moles of sulfur, which equal the moles of SO₂, then use V = nRT/P.

exercises.prompt: Calculate the density of Freon 12, CF<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>, at 30.0 °C and 0.954 atm.

answer.hint: Find the molar mass of CF₂Cl₂ and use d = ℳP/RT.

exercises.prompt: Which is denser at the same temperature and pressure, dry air or air saturated with water vapor? Explain.

answer.solution: Suggested approach: at the same temperature and pressure, a liter of either gas holds the same number of moles, so the denser gas is the one whose average molar mass is greater. Compare the molar mass of water, about 18 g/mol, with those of nitrogen and oxygen, which make up nearly all of dry air, and consider what happens to the average when some of those molecules are replaced by water molecules.

exercises.prompt: A cylinder of O2(g) used in breathing by patients with emphysema has a volume of 3.00 L at a pressure of 10.0 atm. If the temperature of the cylinder is 28.0 °C, what mass of oxygen is in the cylinder?

answer.hint: Find the moles from n = PV/RT, then multiply by the molar mass of O₂.

exercises.prompt: What is the molar mass of a gas if 0.281 g of the gas occupies a volume of 125 mL at a temperature 126 °C and a pressure of 777 torr?

answer.hint: Use ℳ = mRT/PV with the volume in liters, the pressure in atm and the temperature in K.

exercises.prompt: How could you show experimentally that the molecular formula of propene is C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, not CH<sub>2</sub>?

answer.solution: Suggested approach: the two formulas have the same composition by mass, so an analysis of the elements cannot tell them apart; what differs is the molar mass. Measure the mass, pressure, volume and temperature of a sample of the gas, as in Example 9.12, calculate its molar mass from ℳ = mRT/PV, and compare it with the mass of the empirical formula, 14 g/mol, to find how many CH<sub>2</sub> units make up a molecule.

exercises.prompt: The density of a certain gaseous fluoride of phosphorus is 3.93 g/L at STP. Calculate the molar mass of this fluoride and determine its molecular formula.

answer.hint: Rearrange d = ℳP/RT to ℳ = dRT/P, then find the formula PFₓ with that molar mass.

exercises.prompt: A 36.0–L cylinder of a gas used for calibration of blood gas analyzers in medical laboratories contains 350 g CO<sub>2</sub>, 805 g O<sub>2</sub>, and 4,880 g N<sub>2</sub>. At 25 degrees C, what is the pressure in the cylinder in atmospheres?

answer.hint: Convert each mass to moles, add them, and use P = nRT/V.

exercises.prompt: A sample of gas isolated from unrefined petroleum contains 90.0% CH<sub>4</sub>, 8.9% C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, and 1.1% C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> at a total pressure of 307.2 kPa. What is the partial pressure of each component of this gas? (The percentages given indicate the percent of the total pressure that is due to each component.)

parts.hint: Each partial pressure is its fraction of the total pressure.

answer.solution: CH<sub>4</sub>: 276 kPa; C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>: 27 kPa; C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>: 3.4 kPa

exercises.prompt: Most mixtures of hydrogen gas with oxygen gas are explosive. However, a mixture that contains less than 3.0 % O<sub>2</sub> is not. If enough O<sub>2</sub> is added to a cylinder of H<sub>2</sub> at 33.2 atm to bring the total pressure to 34.5 atm, is the mixture explosive?

answer.hint: The partial pressure of the oxygen is the increase in total pressure; its mole fraction is that share of the total.

exercises.prompt: A sample of carbon monoxide was collected over water at a total pressure of 756 torr and a temperature of 18 °C. What is the pressure of the carbon monoxide? (See Table 9.2 for the vapor pressure of water.)

answer.hint: Subtract the vapor pressure of water at 18 °C from the total pressure.

exercises.prompt:
Joseph Priestley first prepared pure oxygen by heating mercuric oxide, HgO:
$2\text{HgO}(s)\;\longrightarrow \;2\text{Hg}(l)+{\text{O}}_{2}(g)$
(a) Outline the steps necessary to answer the following question: What volume of O2 at 23 °C and 0.975 atm is produced by the decomposition of 5.36 g of HgO?
(b) Answer the question.

answer.hint: Moles of HgO, then moles of O₂ from the equation, then V = nRT/P.
answer.solution: (a) Determine the moles of HgO that decompose; using the chemical equation, determine the moles of O<sub>2</sub> produced by decomposition of this amount of HgO; and determine the volume of O<sub>2</sub> from the moles of O<sub>2</sub>, temperature, and pressure. (b) 0.308 L

exercises.prompt:
The chlorofluorocarbon CCl2F2 can be recycled into a different compound by reaction with hydrogen to produce CH2F2(g), a compound useful in chemical manufacturing:
${\text{CCl}}_{2}{\text{F}}_{2}(g)+4{\text{H}}_{2}(g)\;\longrightarrow \;{\text{CH}}_{2}{\text{F}}_{2}(g)+2\text{HCl}(g)$
(a) Outline the steps necessary to answer the following question: What volume of hydrogen at 225 atm and 35.5 °C would be required to react with 1 ton (1.000 × 103 kg) of CCl2F2?
(b) Answer the question.

answer.hint: Moles of CCl₂F₂, four times as many moles of H₂, then V = nRT/P.
answer.solution: (a) Determine the molar mass of CCl<sub>2</sub>F<sub>2</sub>. From the balanced equation, calculate the moles of H<sub>2</sub> needed for the complete reaction. From the ideal gas law, convert moles of H<sub>2</sub> into volume. (b) 3.72 × 10<sup>3</sup> L

exercises.prompt:
Lime, CaO, is produced by heating calcium carbonate, CaCO3; carbon dioxide is the other product.
(a) Outline the steps necessary to answer the following question: What volume of carbon dioxide at 875 K and 0.966 atm is produced by the decomposition of 1 ton (1.000 × 103 kg) of calcium carbonate?
(b) Answer the question.

answer.hint: One mole of CO₂ forms for each mole of CaCO₃; then V = nRT/P.
answer.solution: (a) Balance the equation. Determine the grams of CO<sub>2</sub> produced and the number of moles. From the ideal gas law, determine the volume of gas. (b) 7.43 × 10<sup>5</sup> L

exercises.prompt: Calculate the volume of oxygen required to burn 12.00 L of ethane gas, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, to produce carbon dioxide and water, if the volumes of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> and O<sub>2</sub> are measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.

answer.hint: Balance the combustion of ethane; the volumes react in the ratio of the coefficients.

exercises.prompt:
Consider the following questions:
(a) What is the total volume of the CO2(g) and H2O(g) at 600 °C and 0.888 atm produced by the combustion of 1.00 L of C2H6(g) measured at STP?
(b) What is the partial pressure of H2O in the product gases?

parts.hint: Find the moles of ethane at STP and the moles of products from the balanced equation, then V = nRT/P.
The partial pressure of water is its mole fraction of the products times the total pressure.

exercises.prompt: What volume of oxygen at 423.0 K and a pressure of 127.4 kPa is produced by the decomposition of 129.7 g of BaO<sub>2</sub> to BaO and O<sub>2</sub>?

answer.hint: Balance 2BaO₂ → 2BaO + O₂, find the moles of O₂, then V = nRT/P.

exercises.prompt:
Ethanol, C2H5OH, is produced industrially from ethylene, C2H4, by the following sequence of reactions:
$3{\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{4}+2{\text{H}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}\;\longrightarrow \;{\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5}{\text{HSO}}_{4}+{({\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5})}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}$
${\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5}{\text{HSO}}_{4}+{({\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5})}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}+3{\text{H}}_{2}\text{O}\;\longrightarrow \;3{\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5}\text{OH}+2{\text{H}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}$
What volume of ethylene at STP is required to produce 1.000 metric ton (1000 kg) of ethanol if the overall yield of ethanol is 90.1%?

answer.hint: One mole of ethylene gives one mole of ethanol overall; divide by the yield and use 22.4 L/mol at STP.

exercises.prompt: A sample of a compound of xenon and fluorine was confined in a bulb with a pressure of 18 torr. Hydrogen was added to the bulb until the pressure was 72 torr. Passage of an electric spark through the mixture produced Xe and HF. After the HF was removed by reaction with solid KOH, the final pressure of xenon and unreacted hydrogen in the bulb was 36 torr. What is the empirical formula of the xenon fluoride in the original sample? (Note: Xenon fluorides contain only one xenon atom per molecule.)
